svg.title: How youtube vision picks frames
svg.desc: An 18-minute example video with six chapters, including a sponsor chapter. Step 1: timed caption passages are scored by how well they represent their chapter; the sponsor chapter is skipped, and every other chapter contributes its best passage before any contributes a second, up to six windows. Step 2: only those windows are decoded, one frame per second, from 2 seconds before to 5 seconds after each passage, about 3 of 18 minutes. Step 3: in one zoomed window, cuts split the samples into shots; a close-up face shot is a last resort, a one-frame flash is too short, and a screen-recording shot wins because it overlaps the caption passage longest; its sharp, steady, most typical frame at 8:35 is chosen. Step 4: chosen frames are published as timestamped two-column collages under .cache/youtube-toolkit/vision/<datetime>-<video-id>/ with JSON measurements for each frame, and the downloaded video is deleted. Without usable timed captions, evenly spaced 30-second windows replace step 1. No model API or speech-to-text is used.

g.text: An 18-minute example with chapters. Timed captions and local image analysis only: no model API, no speech-to-text.
Each bar is a caption passage,
one pick before any gets two.

and each shot offers its most
Six frames per page, in time

Scores explain each pick; they are not confidence values.
